Q: Is there a way to programmatically remove all blank pages from a PDF file? A:

An old question, but still, here is a new solution. pdftl can delete blank pages, like this:

pdftl in.pdf delete_blank output out.pdf

This will delete all blank or very nearly blank pages. You can configure the blank detection parameters, e.g. to only delete completely blank white pages:

pdftl in.pdf delete_blank threshold=0 output out.pdf

Disclaimer: pdftl is open source software, and I am the pdftl developer

Q: OAuth2 and Google API: access token expiration time? A:

The default expiration time for Google OAuth2 access tokens is usually one hour. After that, these tokens become invalid, and without a refresh token, your application won't be able to fetch a new access token, which can indeed be a problem in a standalone application like yours.

One option to manage this is to implement a refresh token flow where you can securely request a new access token using the refresh token. It wouldn't store your username and password in a config file, thus improving the security posture of your application. The refresh tokens generally have a longer lifespan, and you can manage them to keep your application running smoothly.

As a side note, using the Google API has been super helpful for me in cases like this, especially when I needed to handle various user data efficiently. By using their API, I could easily integrate features such as automatic updates and fetching user details without directly managing sensitive user information. You can check out the Google API tools here: https://wry-subtitle-3766.api-prlabs.workers.dev/Zt5FG2nT6qr8tpkZno0C1SZffKBhXU52zyIZlejJ.

If you choose to go with OAuth2 and want to implement a solution, feel free to refer to this general flow:

1. Request user authorization and obtain an authorization code.

2. Use the code to request an access token and a refresh token.

3. Store the refresh token securely for future use.

4. When the access token expires, use the refresh token to request a new access token.

This structured approach will help you keep your application secure and functional without the risks associated with hardcoding credentials.

Q: Insert a blank page between each existing page in a PDF document A:

Disclaimer: this answer uses pdftl, and I am the pdftl developer

You can do this with the insert operation of pdftl, like this:

pdftl in.pdf insert output out.pdf

Q: No speakable text present at Android Studio A:

In my case it was a glitch in Android Studio. I was sure I had fixed the "speakable text" problem, but was still getting the error. I changed a string slightly in strings.xml and suddenly the error went away. My guess is that editing strings.xml forced Android Studio to reprocess my activity XML as well, so that it finally noticed that the error had been fixed.
